results.quantity: Q3b: kinematic test: outflow vs disk/warp/tidal feature at Soutflow
results.value: PV diagrams (out/q3b/q3b_pv.png, kin_ns_cuts.csv, kin_ew_cuts.csv). (1) The "sharp red edge" is NOT diagnostic: the 25%-of-peak red edge is 2867-2872 km/s at Soutflow, 2867-2889 at S and 2832-2889 along the N-S cut at x=-0.2": the lobe has no gas redder than the S disk red edge, i.e. it is one-sided (blue only), not specifically cut at Vsys+100. (2) E-W rotation gradient at the S declination 35 km/s/arcsec (v0=2795): expected line sigma for disk gas on the minor axis from beam smearing ~62 km/s, observed 130-150 (HCN) / 112-135 (HCO+) at Soutflow vs 24 at the W control (-4.4,-4.5) and 49-104 at the mirror N of S: the broadening is not rotation smearing. (3) HCO+/HCN peak velocity at Soutflow is 2806-2814, i.e. at the disk systemic velocity (narrow component, sigma 32), plus a broad blue-only skirt: centroid offset -125 km/s relative to the rotation-curve value (2769-2789); the skirt grows with distance from S (N-S centroid 2754 at -2.7", 2629 at -4.5", edge of emission ~-5.9"). (4) No blue tail at the mirror position N of S (blue half HCN 0.027+-0.006 vs 0.215+-0.010 Jy/beam km/s at Soutflow) nor at the W control, E control empty. (5) At 0.5" (Xb4b) the S-lobe pixel velocities scatter by 113 (HCO+)-262 (HCN) km/s rms with only a weak N-S gradient (+44+-5 / +27+-2 km/s/arcsec, r=0.15-0.21; E-W gradient -28..+15), i.e. clumps with up to ~100-250 km/s relative motions on <100 pc, not a smooth gradient (disk gradients here <~45 km/s/arcsec). Which predictions: a smooth warp/tidal arm predicts line widths set by the beam-smeared gradient (~60 km/s), velocities continuous with the E-W curve, and symmetric red/blue clumps; the data show one-sided broad blue gas with sigma 100-150 km/s, centroid shifted -100..-250 km/s and clump-to-clump scatter >100 km/s, which prefers an outflow/entrained or strongly perturbed gas. Not rejected: a tilted-ring warp with a PA twist and v_rot~250 km/s could project -100..-300 km/s on the minor axis, and a tidal feature. Classification stays MEDIUM: more consistent with the dense-gas blue lobe of the S outflow (position/direction match Sakamoto+2014 and Michiyama+2018) than an isolated cloud, but disk-warp/tidal origin is an unrejected alternative.

results.quantity: Q4: Why is S low in HCN/HCO+ (0.37-0.46)? Which of opacity, IR pumping, HCO+ enhancement is supported
results.value: Evidence at S: (1) IR pumping: HCN v2=1f/v=0 <0.05-0.09 (3 sigma, 3-2, 4-3, 0.24-6"), no vibrational excitation -> pumping that raises HCN is not seen (and would raise, not lower, the ratio). (2) Opacity: peak Tb ratio 0.46+-0.04 at 0.24" with equal widths implies tau(HCN 3-2)<~0.7 if HCO+ is thick, vs N 0.93 (both thick/equal); H13CN gives no constraint (R>8, RADEX insensitive). (3) HCO+ enhancement (X-ray/cosmic-ray ionisation): HOC+/HCO+ <0.10 (Xb4d) / <0.035 (Xb4f) at S, N tentatively 0.03-0.05: not diagnostic; CH3OH, SO, CS, H2CS are all weaker relative to HCO+ at S than at N or at the Bridge (CS/HCO+ 0.047 vs 0.081; H2CS 0.039 vs 0.084), consistent with HCO+ being bright rather than HCN faint (a global HCN deficit would not lower CS). Supported: S has HCN that is less thick/less excited than N (HCN thin-ish, HCO+ bright); not distinguishable: lower HCN abundance vs HCO+ enhancement. Shock chemistry is not indicated at the nuclei (CH3OH/SO limits), only in the extended 6" gas (CH3OH at S/Soutflow/Bridge, SiS at S/Soutflow, 6" beam).

interpretation: Line inventory (corrected): besides HCN and HCO+ (J=2-1,3-2,4-3) and CS 7-6, CH3OH is detected (Band 5 165 GHz Q-branch J=1-3 at 27 sigma; 2(0)-1(-1) E at 254.015 GHz at 10 sigma), SO 5(4)-4(3) (Band 5, 8 sigma) is detected, HOC+ is tentative; everything else is a limit, blended or an edge artefact. CH3OH is cold/subthermal (Q-branch J>=4 and Eu>45 K lines absent; LTE Trot~9 K, but LTE and RADEX fits are poor) and extended: the Xb4d (0.9") CH3OH flux is only ~55% of the 9"-beam value, and in Xb4d it peaks on the Bridge and a W clump, not on the N and S nuclei (CH3OH/HCO+ 0.05 there vs <0.015 at the nuclei) - a shock/low-excitation tracer signature that agrees qualitatively with Harada+2018. The extended disk is defined (Xb55 HCO+ 2-1 S/N>5 at r>8", HCN/HCO+(2-1)=0.51) but is not detected in the 3-2/4-3 data with the available sensitivity/zero-level. The southern blue-shifted component 1.9" south of S is statistically solid (7-12 sigma after null calibration, 0 null peaks above 8 sigma in 583 beams), has no red counterpart, is not a PSF-sidelobe copy of S, and has HCN/HCO+(3-2)~1.8 versus 0.4 at S; it is a separate broad component at ~2560-2650 km/s. The N and S nuclei are separable in Xb4b, Xb4d, Xb4f, Xb47 (not in Band 5). The opacity test (H13CN) can only give HCN/H13CN>7-9 (conditional on the CO-wing model). Raw HCN/HCO+ (3-2) peak ratios (N 0.6-1.0, S 0.4-0.5) are preliminary and not beam matched across OUS (Q1). Q1 (rev. 2): At matched 1.05" the northern nucleus has HCN/HCO+ 3-2 = 0.83+-0.04 and the southern (AGN) nucleus 0.40+-0.02 (N/S = 2.0-2.1, constant over the line core, insensitive to the velocity window to <=2.5% and to Xb4b vs Xb4d); the AGN has the lowest ratio, i.e. no HCN enhancement at the AGN (as Harada+2018). Blended 6.5"/10" aperture ratios hide this (N/S 1.1-1.2), but deblending the native-beam Band 7 4-3 map with the 1" templates recovers N/S = 1.9+-0.5 (N 0.47, S 0.25) and CS 7-6 tracks HCO+ (N=S) not HCN; at 2-1 (9" beam) the N-S pair is not separable (contrast 1-3, template-limited). The ladders (3-2/2-1, 4-3/3-2: HCN 0.35/0.39 (N), HCO+ 0.43/0.48) are strongly sub-thermal and the same at N and S within 14% (HCN 4-3/3-2 lower at S, 1.8 sigma): a quick RADEX grid gives n(H2) <~ 1e5 cm-3 and Tkin >~ 30 K at N, and requires N(HCN)/N(HCO+) >= 3 at both nuclei; since the ladders do not differ, the factor-2 N/S HCN/HCO+ contrast must come mainly from the HCN/HCO+ abundance (or HCN column/opacity) rather than density or temperature (equal-X disfavoured at ~2 sigma only). The disk 2-1 HCN/HCO+ is 0.47-0.50, 15-25% below the nuclei at the same beam; its 3-2 deficit is fully consistent with missing short spacings in Xb4f for a 13-14" scale structure (B_min = 8.7 m assumed), so no excitation difference of the disk can be claimed from HCO+; the HCN 3-2 deficit is larger than recovery alone explains but depends on the zero level. The Soutflow blue-wing HCN/HCO+ is 1.2-1.8 depending on estimator (candidate, single position, HCO+ wing 5-7 sigma). Resolution forces an 'active region versus disk' comparison at J=2-1 and for the disk, but not at J=3-2 and 4-3, where N and S are distinguishable. Q3 (outflow, revised): dense gas (HCN 12.6 sigma, HCO+ 5 sigma) is detected 1.9" (370 pc) S of the S nucleus at the blue lobe of the southern edge-on outflow (MEDIUM confidence; a disk warp/tidal feature is not rejected). In fixed a-priori apertures with velocity relative to the local centroid the blue-half HCN/HCO+ 3-2 ratio is 1.0-1.4, robustly above S (0.15-0.46) but not significantly different from N (1.13) and Bridge (1.3); the earlier 1.7 was peak-selected (+10% noise bias, rest spatial gradient); the whole broad component has 0.72-0.8 (N-like). Blends (CH3NH2, CH2NH, CH3CHO, CH3SH, CH3OH) are limited to <=10-18% of the HCN blue side by LTE fits to other lines; HDO untestable. No dense-gas wing at N: 3 sigma <2-4% (HCN, blue 225-750 km/s) of core, mass <=1.3e6-1.4e7 Msun; weak 2-3 sigma hints at North-OF-Blue are not significant. Soutflow dense mass 1.4-6.5e6 Msun (alpha 3-10), ~6-37% of the S-outflow CO high-velocity mass depending on X20. Q4 (opacity and shock tracers): the H13CN 4-3 limits (HCN/H13CN >8 at N and S, >5 Bridge) bound tau(HCN 4-3) only if Tex are equal (<4-12), and RADEX shows they exclude none of the ladder-allowed solutions, so HCN opacity is NOT measured by H13CN; the ladder solutions have tau(HCN 3-2) of order 10-40 (thick), but the data cannot fix N(HCN). At 0.24" the peak Tb ratio HCN/HCO+ is 0.93 at N (consistent with both thick) and 0.46 at S (HCN thin-ish if HCO+ is thick). No IR pumping (v2=1f/v=0 <3-9%). SO is cold/sub-thermal (Trot<=12 K in the 9x6" beam), CH3OH and SiS appear only in extended gas at the Bridge/S-extension/Soutflow in 6" beams and not at the nuclei (<0.013/<0.017 of HCO+); the Band-5 CH3OH Q-branch excess of 1.5-2x is not a maser signature (no inversion in RADEX, normal profile) and is consistent with cold extended CH3OH if Xb4f resolves out half the flux. S being HCO+-bright rather than HCN-faint is favoured by CS and H2CS also being weak relative to HCO+ at S, but HCN under-abundance vs HCO+ enhancement is not separable with these data.
caveats: Peak-pixel intensities use different native beams per OUS; no cross-OUS ratio in this item is beam matched (Q1/Q6).

Systemic velocity 2780 km/s is a single adopted value; nuclear peak velocities differ by ~100 km/s at 0.25" (N 2811-2817, S 2710), so +-350 km/s windows are not centred on each nucleus; the HCN/HCO+ integrals use the same fixed window for both lines.

Line identifications rest on Splatalogue CDMS/JPL rest frequencies at v=2780 km/s; HOC+, SO 4_5-3_4 and both unidentified features need independent confirmation (e.g. matching J transitions at matched beam).
The Band-5 cubes do not separate N, S, Bridge (13% leakage at the nuclear separation, single HCO+ 2-1 peak pixel).
Empirical noise comes from emission-free pixels at 6-11" (primary-beam-corrected noise there is 1.2-1.6x the central value), which makes limits conservative by up to ~1.5x.
Xb4b nuclear emission is clumpy: peak-pixel values depend on the exact pixel chosen (search radius 1"); spectra are non-Gaussian (double-horned), Gaussian FWHM are indicative only.
No source of data for line-free-channel continuum from cubes exists (cubes are continuum-subtracted); the contamination check relies on mfs vs cont images, which have 1-2 sigma noise.
The 'aperture' (1.5" radius) rows of the line table use statistical noise only (no empirical null).
The conversion to K km/s uses the Rayleigh-Jeans formula with the beam of each cube; distance 40 Mpc is only used for pc sizes.

CH3OH LTE/RADEX fits have chi2/dof ~9-11: the numbers Trot=9 K and n>=1e7 are formal; the robust statement is 'Q-branch J>=4 absent: low excitation'. Baseline ripple of ~0.2 K km/s is visible in Band 5 (J=5 at -4 sigma).
Local-velocity matching (not 2780 km/s) is essential for identifications at S (2710-2740 km/s): at vsys the 251.66 feature would favour NS; at local velocity it clearly favours CH3OH.

The zero level of Xb4f/Xb55 moment-0 maps at r>8" is biased by about -0.5 / -1.3 Jy/b km/s (negative bowl, missing short spacings); disk fluxes are zero-level-corrected with the r=14-22" ring and carry >=0.3 Jy/b km/s systematic.

Soutflow position error is dominated by the assumed 10% beam pointing floor (0.10"), not by the fit (0.01-0.02"); wing definition relative to v_S=2722; comparison with the CO outflow geometry (Sakamoto+2014, Michiyama+2018) has not been made quantitatively.
H13CN limit conditional on the CO-wing family; log-quadratic/cubic wings can absorb a genuine H13CN signal.
Literature cross-check is from abstracts/summaries (Harada+2018, Sato+2022), not their tables.

Q1: ratio uncertainties are dominated by systematics (window truncation ~5%, absolute flux scale 10% per band); statistical errors are <=1% at the nuclei. Noise uses few line-free windows contaminated at times by weak lines (quietest quartile used), so faint-region limits are approximate.
Q1: regions use fixed nominal positions; the N ratio varies across its sub-clumps (IQR 0.05-0.09 at 1.05"), so a different aperture centre changes N by ~0.03-0.05.

Q1: the decline of HCN/HCO+ and the low 3-2/2-1, 4-3/3-2 ladder ratios at 10" mix Band 5, 6 and 7 data with different resolved-out fractions (Q6: Xb4f is the most complete Band 6 set); they should be treated as inputs to RADEX with 14% errors, not as evidence for a nuclear difference.

Q1: the Xb55 2-1 "disk" may include beam wings of the nuclei and NEclump; the ring zero level (-1.2 to -2.0 Jy/b km/s) is not present in line-free channels, so the sign of the correction is uncertain.

Q1b: the deblending assumes a uniform ratio inside each template component and that the 1" 3-2 template traces the same gas as the coarse line; chi2_r of the fits is 7-44 even with a 3% floor, so formal errors are meaningless and template systematics (a factor ~2 on N/S flux ratios at 2-1) dominate. Only the 4-3 N/S HCN/HCO+ contrast (1.9+-0.5) survives the injection test.

Q1b: the disk recovery model assumes B_min and a single Gaussian disk; the array identity is inferred from beam sizes (no uv information in the products). The zero-level (ring) correction of the disk maps changes the 3-2 ratio by a factor of 4, so disk 3-2 statements are limits.

Q1b: RADEX constraints come from 5 ratios and 4 parameters (1 dof), assume equal beam filling for all lines and a single (n, T) per region for HCN and HCO+; they bound n(H2) and X, not the absolute columns. The H13CN limit is conditional on the CO-wing model of p0001.

Q3 (round 2): outflow classification rests on kinematics (one-sided broad blue gas, mirror/control positions) and literature geometry, not CO; disk-warp/tidal origin unrejected. Blend limits cover CH3NH2, CH3OH, CH2NH, CH3CHO, CH3SH only (HDO and exotic species untested) and assume HCO+-like profiles. Xb4b (independent array) gives lower ratios (blue half 0.9-1.0 vs 1.2-1.4) and recovers ~55% of the flux: ratio systematics 10-25%. Noise is statistical (flux scale 5-10% common to all positions). The two-Gaussian split is shape-dependent (chi2/dof 2.6). N limits are for compact gas at 225-750 km/s LOS only; HCO+ red window contaminated by HCN v2=1f; HCN red window truncated at +693 km/s by the band edge. Dense masses: alpha 3-10 and r31 0.3-1 are assumptions; CO mass comparison uses the whole S-outflow CO HV mass (both lobes) so fractions are good to a factor ~2 only. RADEX is illustrative (no dof).

Q4: H13CN is on the red wing of CO 3-2 (core out of band); detection at N (alpha 0.03-0.075) depends on the wing model; a limit is quoted. The equal-Tex tau bound is invalid in sub-thermal gas (RADEX): the earlier Q1b "tau43<=5.5" shortcut should be read with this caveat.

Q4: HCN v2=1f limits assume equal beam filling and thin vib line; IR pumping in a source much smaller than 47 pc would be diluted in all beams. SO 4_5-3_4 flux changed from 1.25 Jy/beam km/s (peak pixel, no wing subtraction) to 0.63+-0.08 K km/s (=0.97 Jy/beam km/s at 9.4x6.3") after fitting the HCO+ wing; Band-5 SO is blended N+S+Bridge. CH3OH maser test depends on the unknown flux recovery of Xb4f relative to Band 5; the 6_5-5_4 SO temperature limit scales the same way. HOC+ and HC15N hints are 3-3.5 sigma only. To settle: HCO+/H13CO+ or HC18O+ (not in band), matched 1-0 lines, and short-spacing Band 6 data.
